newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian stocks drift in directionless trade.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian stocks drift in directionless trade.

text.p: Norwegian stocks drifted lower on Tuesday in directionless trade with little impulses from overseas markets. The Total share index close off 0.2 percent at 1,070.54 points in turnover of 994 million crowns.
Direction was negative in all sectors except for banking, which remained in a positive trend begun last week following a period of lagging the rest of the market.

The banking index ended 1.03 percent higher at 103.45 points with the two largest commercial banks -- Den norske Bank and Christiania og Kreditkasse -- being among the top ten traded shares of the day in value terms.
Telecommunications group Nera took a dip after its financial results for 1996 came in below expectations.

Nera attributed higher R&D expenditure and non-recurring costs for restructuring and expansion to a six percent fall in operating profits to 171.9 million crowns compared with a year ago. Pre-tax income was down nearly nine percent at 140.4 million crowns against 153.7 million crowns.
But a healthy order backlog and high production capacity pointed to a positive development in 1997, Nera said.
Nera was the most traded share in turnover of 97.2 million crowns, closing 7.50 crowns down at 304.50 crowns.
